topic: AI Agent Deployment Infrastructure Guide 2026: Ampere.sh, E2B, Northflank, and Modal Compared
keyword: AI agent deployment infrastructure hosting comparison 2026

key_points: Ranks Northflank, E2B, Modal, Fly.io Sprites, and Vercel Sandbox as Runloop alternatives for AI agent sandbox infrastructure.
Strong comparison axes: isolation model, persistent versus ephemeral environments, BYOC availability, compliance, GPU support, and whether the platform is sandbox-only or a full workload runtime.
Positions Northflank as a full-stack workload platform with self-serve BYOC, microVM/gVisor/Kata isolation, GPUs, databases, workers, APIs, and sandboxes in one control plane.
Useful SERP pattern: clear TL;DR, decision matrix by requirement, cost-at-scale table, and FAQ targeting procurement/security questions.
Frames E2B as purpose-built for AI agent code execution and Modal as a broader serverless compute platform that includes sandboxes.
Distinguishes E2B's session/template model from Modal's runtime-defined container model and GPU/serverless infrastructure scope.
Useful gap: article is vendor-positioned and does not cover managed agent hosting products like Ampere.sh as a different category.
Defines sandbox providers by category: AI code execution, network/security sandboxing, and developer environment sandboxes.
Reinforces evaluation criteria that matter for production AI agents: isolation technology, cold-start definition, persistence, BYOC, compliance, and platform scope.
Provides pricing and BYOC comparison patterns that readers expect in this SERP.
Official E2B docs explicitly target coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Amp.
E2B's core value proposition is a full Linux environment with terminal, filesystem, git, templates, parallel sandboxes, and result extraction.
Best fit is SDK-driven agent execution where each task needs an isolated dev machine rather than a full app deployment platform.
Official Modal docs describe sandboxes as secure containers for executing untrusted user or agent code.
Modal's differentiator is broader serverless infrastructure: custom images, volumes, secrets, readiness probes, tunnels, GPU options, and Python-first cloud execution.
Best fit is teams already using Modal for AI/ML workloads or needing GPU-backed serverless jobs plus sandbox execution.
Ampere.sh is not a general-purpose sandbox API; it is managed hosting for OpenClaw agents with one-click setup.
Claims to handle OpenClaw hosting, model routing, browser automation, memory, web search, backups, updates, BYOK, and marketplace skills.
Best fit is users who want a hosted always-on personal or workflow agent, not teams building their own sandbox substrate.

stats.fact: E2B documents coding-agent support for Claude Code, Codex, Amp, and OpenCode, giving each agent an isolated Linux environment with terminal, filesystem, git, and pre-built templates.
E2B's BYOC documentation says BYOC is currently available only for AWS and Google Cloud, with Azure planned, and is limited to Enterprise customers who contact the E2B team.
Modal's sandbox documentation says sandboxes can execute untrusted user or agent code, define containers at runtime, run generated code, check out git repositories, and execute test or lint commands.
Modal sandboxes have a default maximum lifetime of 5 minutes and can be configured up to 24 hours; longer workflows are directed toward filesystem snapshots.

Modal's LLM guidance says Modal is a serverless cloud platform designed for AI/ML workloads but usable for general-purpose cloud compute, with Functions, Classes, Sandboxes, Volumes, Secrets, Dicts, and Queues as core concepts.

Northflank's Runloop alternatives article claims Northflank supports Firecracker, Kata Containers, and gVisor-backed sandbox infrastructure, ephemeral and persistent environments, self-serve BYOC, SOC 2 Type 2 compliance, APIs/workers/databases/jobs, and on-demand GPUs in one platform.

Northflank's comparison states E2B offers Python and JavaScript SDKs, pause/resume with state preservation, snapshots, SSH, terminal, proxy tunneling, custom domains, git integration, and cloud storage bucket connectivity.

Northflank's comparison states Modal sandboxes use gVisor-based isolation, support custom container images, configurable sandbox timeouts up to 24 hours, GPU access, tunnels, egress policies, and filesystem snapshots.

Ampere.sh positions itself as managed OpenClaw hosting: deploy an OpenClaw agent in 60 seconds with no server setup or maintenance, including browser automation, memory, web search, BYOK, backups, and marketplace skills.
Ampere.sh's public pricing page lists Pro at $39/month with 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM, 40GB storage, and Ultra at $79/month with 8 vCPU, 16GB RAM, and 80GB storage, plus a custom Business tier.

angles: Separate three categories that competitors blur together: managed personal-agent hosting (Ampere.sh), agent sandbox APIs (E2B), and cloud workload runtimes with sandbox primitives (Modal and Northflank).
The right platform depends on what the agent must own: a chat/workflow identity, an isolated coding workspace, a GPU job, or a production deployment plane.
Ampere.sh should be framed as the fastest path to running OpenClaw, not a substitute for E2B or Modal when developers need programmable sandbox orchestration.
E2B is the strongest fit for coding-agent workspaces because it is built around full Linux machines, git, templates, SDK control, pause/resume, and extraction of diffs or artifacts.
Modal is strongest when sandbox execution is only one part of a larger AI/ML compute stack that also needs GPUs, batch jobs, volumes, secrets, queues, or hosted endpoints.

Northflank is the enterprise/platform-engineering option when BYOC, compliance, persistent environments, production services, databases, workers, and sandboxes need to share one operational control plane.
Buying criteria should include isolation model, persistence, session timeout, BYOC, GPU support, deployment scope, secret handling, observability, pricing model, and operational owner.
A defensible article should warn that vendor comparison posts are often self-positioned; verify pricing, limits, BYOC availability, and compliance status on current vendor pages before committing.

The SEO opportunity is to answer 'where do I deploy AI agents?' more broadly than existing sandbox-provider posts, which often ignore managed OpenClaw-style hosting and full production deployment needs.
Use workload examples: coding agent PR review, browser automation worker, multi-tenant user code execution, autonomous personal assistant, GPU inference agent, and enterprise BYOC agent runtime.
